title: SmallObjectSlab arena churn 的泛化性裁决
verdict_scope: The churn phenomenon does generalise to any transient allocation in a size class whose free-arena list is empty, but it generalises to qjs equally: the policy, constants and backing allocator are identical, and qjs churns at the same or a higher rate. It therefore does not generalise as a zjs-vs-qjs alignment defect, and no allocator-layer production line is authorised.

block_header_bytes.note: quickjs.c comment "8 byte header"; zjs alignForward(@sizeOf(BlockHeader)=3, 8)

release_policy.qjs: quickjs.c:1626-1630 list_del x2 + js_free(ar) when n_used_blocks hits 0

backing_allocator.note: zjs links libc, so use_debug_allocator is false and c_allocator is selected

arena_init_cost.zjs: 1 store per block (block_size_idx stamped at pop time)
arena_init_cost.note: zjs arena construction is marginally cheaper per block, not more expensive

mechanism_equivalence.slab_active_note: JS_MALLOC_LARGE_BLOCKS_ONLY is 1 only under __SANITIZE_ADDRESS__; the benchmark build has no ASAN so it is 0

trigger_condition.original_framing: the slab returns its arena as soon as a size class empties
trigger_condition.corrected: an arena is released when that arena reaches zero used blocks, and churn occurs when the class free-arena list is empty at the next allocation
trigger_condition.consequence: a resident population that exactly fills its arenas leaves the free list empty and churns anyway; measured directly (400 residents at 50 blocks/arena still churned, 411 did not)

instrument.why: both engines route arena acquire/release to glibc, so one instrument counts both with no source change
instrument.caveat: a payload allocation landing on one of the 12 arena sizes is counted as an arena; the full histogram is emitted so contamination is visible

baseline_arena_events.note: empty script; subtracted from every case

bigint_localisation.zjs_allocation: src/libs/bigint.zig:742 const u = try allocator.alloc(Limb, na + 1)
bigint_localisation.why_only_one_event_per_division: v (nb limbs -> 40B class) and q (quotient_len limbs -> 48B class) land in populated classes; only u lands in the unpopulated 80B class
bigint_localisation.qjs_counterpart: js_bigint_divrem allocates r = js_bigint_new(na+2) = 10 limbs + 8B JSBigInt header = 88B payload -> 96B class, which is populated

in_situ_control.method: retain 411 Uint8Array(72) -- the JS-reachable shape that allocates in the 80-byte class -- and change nothing about the division

timing.per_event_cost_note: the typed-array A/B on qjs gives 1323 insn / 265 cyc / 67.9 ns per arena acquire+release; the in-situ BigInt figure is 834 insn / 147 cyc / 37.7 ns. The per-event cost is context-dependent and the in-situ number is the one that should be quoted for the division.

refuted_hypothesis.claim: array_map_callback, the largest single item in the P7-20 Pareto, would show the churn
refuted_hypothesis.note: 10,000 map() calls produce 10 net arena events on zjs and 5 on qjs; its 2.618 ratio is not allocator churn
